name: Waama
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Peter-Bremicker, Ursula 1990. Description systematique du waama (langue voltaique du Benin): phonologie, grammaire; also Prost 1972 Le Wama. Neither found online.

new_statements.quote: Cette section présente un bref résumé de points les plus essentiels de l'analyse du système tonal de Peter (1990) dont nos travaux viennent confirmer les grandes lignes, à savoir que le waama comporte deux tons distinctifs, H et B, contrairement aux autres langues gur de la branche oti-volta orientale qui, elles, comportent trois tons sous-jacents. [...] Un premier triage de notre corpus lexical vient confirmer l'interprétation de Peter que c'est la syllabe qui est l'unité porteuse de ton
new_statements.translation: This section gives a brief summary of the most essential points of Peter's (1990) analysis of the tone system, whose broad lines our work confirms, namely that Waama has two distinctive tones, H and L, unlike the other Gur languages of the Eastern Oti-Volta branch, which have three underlying tones. [...] A first sorting of our lexical corpus confirms Peter's interpretation that the syllable is the tone-bearing unit
new_statements.citation: Sandjougouma, Yoro Issacar & David Roberts. 2021. Vers une orthographe appropriée du ton pour le waama. Série électronique de documents de travail, SIL Togo-Bénin 14. Lomé: SIL Togo-Bénin.
new_statements.locator: §2.1 'Survol', p. 4; §3.2 'Unité porteuse du ton', p. 10 (report pagination; PDF pp. 6 and 12)
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (and the 44-page PDF). Both quoted passages are there word for word: "Cette section présente un bref résumé de points les plus essentiels de l'analyse du système tonal de Peter (1990) dont nos travaux viennent confirmer les grandes lignes, à savoir que le waama comporte deux tons distinctifs, H et B, contrairement aux autres langues gur de la branche oti-volta orientale qui, elles, comportent trois tons sous-jacents." (§2.1 Survol, report p. 4) and "Un premier triage de notre corpus lexical vient confirmer l'interprétation de Peter que c'est la syllabe qui est l'unité porteuse de ton" (§3.2, report p. 10). The only difference is the PDF-page locator: report p. 4 is PDF page 5 (not 6)…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Waama is a two-tone language (H, L) with upstep/downstep and floating low tones; the syllable is the tone-bearing unit and lexical tone schemes (HB, ↑HH, HH, BB, BH... on disyllables) are contrastive. No source opened says anything about word stress: none locates a stressed syllable, and none explicitly denies stress. Rowe 1991 (p. 298) independently: 'two phonemic tones, high and low'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: Not applicable (no stress statement). Tone: the 2021 authors found extra noun tone schemes (↑HH, ↓B↓B) beyond Peter's four; Eddyshaw 2024 notes the three tone-marked sources (Sambiéni 2005, Reineke 2012, Pope 2014) disagree on individual words.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone description is at word level (isolated nouns and verbs, then two-word phrases showing tonal mobility). Peter 1990's abstract makes the moneme (morpheme) the TBU; the 2021 report reads her transcription as syllable-based.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Waama proper (wwa, waam1244) of the Natitingou area; the 2021 report (citing Sambiéni 2005) distinguishes the main dialect (Natitingou, Toucountouna, Kouandé) from tangamma (Tanguiéta) but its corpus is not assigned to either. Prost 1972 uses the names Wama / Yoabou for the same language. No separate glottocode for the dialects.

sources.quote: Cette section présente un bref résumé de points les plus essentiels de l'analyse du système tonal de Peter (1990) dont nos travaux viennent confirmer les grandes lignes, à savoir que le waama comporte deux tons distinctifs, H et B, contrairement aux autres langues gur de la branche oti-volta orientale qui, elles, comportent trois tons sous-jacents. [...] Un premier triage de notre corpus lexical vient confirmer l'interprétation de Peter que c'est la syllabe qui est l'unité porteuse de ton
sources.locator: §2.1 'Survol', p. 4; §3.2 'Unité porteuse du ton', p. 10 (report pagination; PDF pp. 6 and 12)
sources.note: Entire report is on tone: two distinctive tones H and B (confirming Peter 1990), upstep/downstep, floating L, tone-bearing unit = syllable (§2.2, §3.2), tone schemes of di-/trisyllabic nouns and verbs (§3.3-3.4). The word 'accent' occurs only for orthographic accent marks; nothing on word stress, prominence or intensity.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 waam1244; WALS wwa (source: Peter 1990); OLAC wwa (5 resources); PHOIBLE waam1244 (inventory AA 838, 41 segments); English Wikipedia 'Waama language'; Omniglot Waama page
sources.note: Aggregators: Wikipedia and Omniglot state two tones (low, high; grave accent = low tone); none says anything about stress.

sources.citation: Eddyshaw, David. 2024. Proto-Oti-Volta: A Work in Progress. Zenodo record 10901653, doi:10.5281/zenodo.7979828.
sources.note: Comparative work. §2.8.3 'Waama' (pp. 101-102): 'The Waama tone system differs considerably from the rest of EOV. Waama tonal data are scanty, and the sources differ'; notes Reineke's informant rejected many tones in Peter-Bremicker's studies, which he could not consult; Pope 2014 has two basic tones. §5.7 Waama historical changes. No statement on Waama stress (its few 'stress' mentions concern Dagaare/Buli).

sources.citation: Pope, Katharina (ed.). 2014. Dictionnaire waama-français (édition préliminaire). SIL International, Webonary (4,786 entries; front matter: Classement alphabétique, Formes de l'entrée, Phonologie, Grammaire pages)
sources.note: Orthography note only: grave accent marks low tone on a few grammatical words (bà 'ils' vs ba negation, ò 'il' vs o 'tu'); homographs distinguished by 'tons phonétiques' in brackets; the 'Phonologie' and 'Grammaire' pages contain only references to Peter-Bremicker 1985/1990. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Rowe, Jennifer L. 1991. The conditional particle ka in Waama. Studies in African Linguistics 22(3): 297-314.
